children: New automatic CNG variants of Swift, Dzire and Baleno are expected to help the carmaker increase sales

Maruti Suzuki India is targeting close to 1 million sales of green vehicles in FY27, covering compressed natural gas (CNG), hybrid and electric vehicles. The carmaker has raised its earlier target of 800,000–900,000 units, with new automatic CNG models expected to help drive demand.

The company has also introduced automatic S-CNG versions of the Swift, Dzire and Baleno under its Auto Green Mission. Maruti Suzuki currently holds around 70 per cent of the CNG passenger vehicle market and sells close to 80,000 CNG vehicles a month.
Maruti Suzuki's new CNG models are aimed at buyers who want lower running costs but do not want to compromise on the convenience of an automatic transmission.

“CNG models previously lost out to petrol/automatic combinations because they lacked automatic transmission options,” said Partho Banerjee, Senior Executive Officer, Marketing and Sales, Maruti Suzuki India.

The Swift automatic S-CNG is priced at Rs 7.92 lakh, while the Baleno automatic S-CNG costs Rs 8.32 lakh. The Dzire automatic S-CNG is priced at Rs 8.53 lakh, with all prices ex-showroom. Maruti Suzuki claims the Dzire automatic S-CNG delivers a fuel efficiency of 36.47 km/kg.
Maruti Suzuki said demand is not currently the main constraint on CNG sales. Instead, the company is limited by production capacity.

Its current CNG production capacity stands at around 18,000 vehicles a month. Banerjee said the company plans to increase supplies as capacity is expanded, which could allow it to sell more CNG vehicles.
CNG accounts for around 43 per cent of Maruti Suzuki's portfolio. The company is therefore relying on its existing CNG customer base as it works towards the 1 million green vehicle target.
The target comes at a time when crude oil prices are around USD 100 a barrel.
